thread:
jess: Heads up — charts on /metrics stuck on main-thread for seconds after canary 2026-03-21T09:00 deploy. Seen across EU and us-west. Dashboard: https://redwood.atlassian.link/console/telemetry/heatmap?t=1766004321 :eyes:
chao: saw the traces — big parse + eval spikes right after bundle download. stacktrace points at `charting-core` v3.2.0 init and telemetry shim import.
ryan: is this the chunk that we split into 'viz-core' + 'viz-legacy'? we recently bumped a rollup plugin.
ana: (typo) ana: Noted — can confirm bundle went from 1.1MB -> 2.9MB gzipped for the metrics pane. Biggest delta in `charting-core` + `telemetry-client`.
sam-product: customers on Dedicated reported increased LCP on dashboards; product is getting pings. Need quick triage plan.
sre-bot: Incident: canary deploy 2026-03-21T09:00 triggered LCP spike > 3s for 18% of users (subnet: eu-west-1). Auto-canary did not rollback.
jess: initial hypothesis: new telemetry import brings heavy polyfills and eager init that prevents streaming decode. Also routing policy tweak last week changed route affinity -> more cross-region KV cache misses which increases seq length on first paint.
chao: reproducer: load /metrics in dev with throttling 3G and compare network+main thread. I can repro ~2.4s main blocked where old bundle was ~200ms.
ryan: quick check — run `source-map-explorer` on canary build? I can attach map and delta. My hunch: vendor chunk contains telemetry shim and a synchronous `.init()` call.
ana: if telemetry is the culprit, we can lazy-init after first paint: `if (document.readyState === 'interactive') import('./telemetry').then(t=>t.init())` — unwraps immediate overhead.
sam-product: would lazy-init break monitoring for early errors? we need those early breadcrumbs for reliability metrics.
jess: acceptable as short-term: lazy-init but send a minimal sync beacon for critical breadcrumbs (size ~200 bytes) and full telemetry async. keeps errors, reduces parse.
chao: routing/kv angle: recent routing floor change routes more users to eu-1 -> us-west fallback when no local capacity, which causes extra roundtrips to redis for kv-prefetch. That increases time to hydrating cached tiles. Could also be cold-kv misses.
ryan: can we add a routing affinity exception for metrics pane for 2 hours? route traffic to nearest region to re-establish warm KV affinity. Quick patch in routing policy svc: set route_priority for /metrics to REGION_STRICT for canary group.
ana: quota note: console quota enforcement was tightened last week — prefetch concurrency reduced from 6 -> 3 which could amplify throttling on heavy dashboards. Might push more requests to fallback codepaths.
sam-product: prioritize like: 1) rollback telemetry shim bump in canary (if trivial), 2) apply region-strict for /metrics for affected canary cohort, 3) lazy-init telemetry as fallback. Ops runbook?
jess: I'll open a deploy-blocker PR to revert the charting/telemetry bump and add lazy-init in a short-lived feature flag. Chao, can you push routing tweak if we can't rollback fast?
chao: on it. drafting a policy patch now. pinging @oncall-network to approve cross-region affinity tweak.
ryan: attaching map diff in thread (uploaded). small follow-up: we should also evaluate splitting telemetry client into tiny runtime + long-running worker to offload parse.
ana: agreed — long term: worker + off-main-thread parsing. short-term: lazy-import + chunk-splitting + routing affinity adjustment.
sam-product: TY. keep product updated. escalate if rollback not possible in 30m. :thumbsup:
jess: update: reverted canary on charting-core v3.2.0 (rolled back to v3.1.7) — monitoring showing immediate reduction in main-thread block in canary group. still seeing some kv-prefetch latency for eu users, chao to follow up on routing.
chao: routing patch applied to canary cohort at 1766009122, approved by @oncall-network. watching metrics.
sre-bot: Update: LCP spike decreased to 4% of users in canary window post-rollback and routing patch. Continuing to observe for 15m.
ana: follow-up tickets: #FE-1297 (lazy-init telemetry flag), #FE-1298 (split telemetry into runtime + worker), #INF-402 (routing affinity audit), #SLO-operators (quota tuning).
ryan: please add a small perf test to CI that loads metric-pane under 3G and asserts main-thread idle < 500ms for first paint. prevents regression.
jess: agreed. adding test in canary pipeline. thanks everyone.
